svg.title: Four Checks Before a Filing Strategy
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-statutory-and-recovery-tree; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Checks Before a Filing Strategy; subtitle: Separate source eligibility, claim detail, procedure, and recovery risk; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: The renderer presents four sequential decision nodes; each detail states its proceed or stop branch. Numerical recovery parameters are sensitivity assumptions, not observed DOJ intervention or Granston-era dismissal rates. Agency and court outcomes require matter-specific assessment.; caption: FCA shares generally run 15%–25% after government intervention and 25%–30% without intervention, subject to statutory exceptions and reductions. SEC and CFTC generally use 10%–30%; IRS § 7623(b) generally uses 15%–30%. No common 15%–30% rate should be applied across programs. Annual operating cash includes zero pending award value.; stages: label: Source Eligibility; value: Check 1: proceed only with defensible eligibility; numeric value: 1.0; detail: For FCA matters, counsel tests 31 U.S.C. § 3730(e)(4), qualifying public disclosures, and original-source requirements; public-data mining alone does not bypass the bar. If unresolved, stop filing preparation and resolve the issue. Separately test SEC or IRS eligibility under its own rules.; label: Claim Particularity; value: Check 2: proceed with adequately supported allegations; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Counsel tests Rule 9(b), applicable circuit standards, and 31 U.S.C. § 3729 elements. Build representative claim links where required: who, what, when, where, amount, payment request, and evidence. If specificity fails, obtain lawful corroboration or stop.; label: Seal and Submission Control; value: Check 3: proceed only through controlled counsel procedure; numeric value: 3.0; detail: FCA complaints remain sealed for at least 60 days under § 3730(b)(2), with court-authorized extensions. Do not serve the defendant before court direction. Seal breaches can cause sanctions or dismissal, but dismissal is not automatic. Restrict access; route SEC TCR and IRS 211 separately through counsel.; label: Zero-Recovery Stress Test; value: Check 4: fund operations without pending recoveries; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Illustrative FCA sensitivity uses intervention i=20%, non-intervention=80%, dismissal conditional on non-intervention d=25%, and positive collection probabilities of 60% after intervention and 20% after non-intervention survival. Collection probability is i*0.60+(1-i)*(1-d)*0.20=24%; zero collection is 76%. A severe case with both collection probabilities at zero yields zero recovery. Model government dismissal, including Granston-policy risk, under § 3730(c)(2)(A); non-intervention itself is not dismissal. Exclude all pending amounts from operating cash regardless of modeled probability.

If unresolved, stop filing preparation and resolve the issue. Separately test SEC or IRS eligibility under its own rules.

rect.title: label: Seal and Submission Control; value: Check 3: proceed only through controlled counsel procedure; numeric value: 3.0; detail: FCA complaints remain sealed for at least 60 days under § 3730(b)(2), with court-authorized extensions. Do not serve the defendant before court direction. Seal breaches can cause sanctions or dismissal, but dismissal is not automatic. Restrict access; route SEC TCR and IRS 211 separately through counsel.
